body: HashMap/RandomState iteration as the Windows/Linux divergence source rejected: each platform repeats its own result bit-for-bit across processes (RandomState reseeds per process); first cross-platform difference is 1-2 ULP in car rotations right after city load, and std f32 atan2/sin/cos differ between UCRT and glibc (sqrt identical).

G1 pass-through (seed 1 node 140, connectors 1284/1293 granted together, bodies overlap 0.184 m while centre lines stay 3.25 m apart): fix the conflict table in graph.rs to use swept car rectangles (TASK-036 item 4) inside this hotfix, rather than defer to TASK-036 and quarantine the gate.

Swept-body conflict table alone: target gates green on both platforms, but traffic_causes::rb_a_box_car_seen_from_afar_is_cleared turns RED on both (Dynamic 98.8 s): the new trajectory parks grant holder 1922v0 on the lane-249 crosswalk with walkers pinned at its nose (recovery: coming_clear false, led true), the node-141 class of TASK-036 item 1 / TASK-037.

Experiment B (reverted): characters at rest relative to a car are ignored by the Character switch and by recovery (nobody_coming, corridor). rb, a_left_car_seed_1/7, c, b3, traffic_contact, go_around, junction_box, gridlock green on Windows; spot_c goes GATE BROKEN (its pressed dummies no longer switch cars). Not shipped: it rewrites the TASK-032 contact contract and re-anchors a gate, beyond small-fix.

Hand back with the conflict-table fix kept and rb red, and ask the orchestrator to choose (A) scope the rb/(a) Dynamic bound like the (c) row with a TASK-036/037 pointer, (B) the resting-walker rule as a full-mode fix, or (C) TASK-036 item 1 first; rather than relax the bound or rewrite the contact contract inside the hotfix.

box_rules::connector_rects centre-line band (body corners reach 0.87-0.91 m past it on right turns) is a real pass-through path via demoted/stuck kinematic bodies, but recommended for TASK-036 item 4 with a G1 fixture rather than this hotfix: swapping in body_sweep shapes changes repick/stuck behaviour (reaches 4 m onto exit lanes) and needs its own measurement.

I5 as prescribed (config floor on conflict_margin tied to BODY_SAMPLE_STEP) rejected: no margin is derivable from the step. Corner step between 0.2 m samples reaches 0.83-0.98 m on right-turn pivots (notch bound up to 0.48 m >> margin/2 0.15), so a rigorous floor would reject the shipped 0.3; yet tables built with margin 0.01/0.1/0.2 show zero unmargined touches under a 0.03 m oracle on seeds 1..8, so any floor would be an invented number. positive() already rejects <= 0. Doc claim corrected instead; the oracle gate carries the guarantee.

I0 option A: one helper dynamic_bound_on(row, approaches, clock) asserts the Dynamic 30 s bound on the scene approach lanes for (a), (c) and rb (rb: every lane ending at the box node) and prints the rest; rather than keeping per-row copies of the (c) partition. rb flip (partition always in-scene) goes RED with the 98.8 s holder.

Verdict NEEDS_FIXES on the (a) row only: the scoped Dynamic bound in abandoned_car hides the original Linux CI failure (sweep off -> 71.05 s stand classified off-scene, a_left_car_seed_1 GREEN) while the city-wide bound is GREEN with the fix on Linux (seeds 1, 7) and RED with the sweep off ('stood 71.0 s'); restore clock.dynamic_violation() for (a) rather than ship the unneeded relaxation. rb/(c) scoping kept as decided (A).

QA F1: causes (a) restored to the city-wide clock.dynamic_violation() instead of keeping the scene-scoped dynamic_bound_on; Linux: GREEN with the sweep clause, RED without it ('an AI car stood 71.0 s in Dynamic'). rb and (c) keep the scene scope per decision A.
